environments.title: General scientific Python
environments.description: NumPy, pandas and SciPy for tables, statistics and numerical work, such as parsing and summarizing QC reports. Every other environment includes these packages too.
use_for: Reading, joining, reshaping and summarizing tables (CSV, TSV, JSON) with pandas
Statistical tests, distributions, regression, optimization and linear algebra with SciPy and NumPy
Parsing and aggregating text reports such as FastQC summaries, samtools flagstat and Picard metrics
Scripts that need only the Python standard library

environments.title: Cheminformatics
environments.description: Small-molecule cheminformatics: RDKit for SMILES and SDF parsing, standardization, descriptors, fingerprints and similarity, substructure and SMARTS search, scaffolds, maximum common substructure, 3D conformers and drawing; mmpdb for matched molecular pair analysis.
use_for: Parse, validate and standardize SMILES, SDF and MOL files
Molecular descriptors and drug-likeness rules (molecular weight, logP, TPSA, Lipinski)
Fingerprints, Tanimoto similarity, clustering and diversity picking of compounds
Substructure and SMARTS searches, Murcko scaffolds, maximum common substructure
3D conformer generation and force-field optimization (ETKDG, MMFF, UFF)
Drawing molecules and grids to PNG or SVG
Matched molecular pair analysis with mmpdb
notes: Draw molecules with rdkit.Chem.Draw; no plotting library is installed.

environments.title: Medical imaging (DICOM and NIfTI)
environments.description: Medical imaging files: pydicom to read, write, inspect and de-identify DICOM, nibabel for NIfTI and other neuroimaging formats, and the dcm2niix command to convert DICOM series to NIfTI with BIDS JSON sidecars.
use_for: Read DICOM headers and pixel data, list series and tags, check acquisition parameters
De-identify or edit DICOM attributes and write new DICOM files
Convert DICOM series to NIfTI (with BIDS sidecars) using dcm2niix
Load, resample, reorient and save NIfTI volumes and compute simple image statistics
notes: Compressed transfer syntaxes that need extra codecs (for example JPEG 2000 through pylibjpeg or GDCM) may not decode.

environments.title: Multi-omics integration
environments.description: Multi-omics integration and pathway analysis: scikit-learn for machine learning, pyComBat (combat) for batch correction, mofapy2 for MOFA+ factor analysis, and GSEApy for GSEA, preranked GSEA, ssGSEA and over-representation analysis against gene sets supplied as files.
use_for: Batch correction of expression or omics matrices with ComBat
Integrating several omics layers into latent factors with MOFA+
Gene set enrichment (GSEA, prerank, ssGSEA, over-representation with gseapy.enrich) against GMT files or dictionaries
Clustering, dimensionality reduction and classifiers with scikit-learn
notes: The sandbox has no internet access, so Enrichr, gseapy.get_library and gene ID mapping services (MyGene.info, biomaRt) are unavailable. Write gene sets to a GMT file and map identifiers before the data reaches the sandbox.
R and Bioconductor (biomaRt, sva, MOFA2, fgsea) are not installed.

environments.title: Bulk RNA-seq differential expression
environments.description: Bulk RNA-seq differential expression: PyDESeq2, a Python implementation of DESeq2 (size factors, dispersion estimates, Wald tests, Benjamini-Hochberg correction, log fold change shrinkage) for gene-level count matrices.
use_for: Differential expression between conditions from a genes x samples count matrix and sample metadata
Normalized counts, variance-stabilized expression and PCA of samples
Volcano and MA plots of DESeq2 results
notes: Read alignment and quantification (STAR, Salmon, featureCounts) are not installed; start from a counts matrix.
R and Bioconductor DESeq2 are not installed.

environments.title: Variant and alignment files (VCF, BAM)
environments.description: Genomic variant and alignment files: pysam to read, filter, annotate and write VCF/BCF, SAM/BAM/CRAM and tabix-indexed files, for example to filter annotated variants by ACMG/AMP criteria.
use_for: Read and filter VCF/BCF records by INFO fields such as gnomAD allele frequency, ClinVar significance, REVEL or CADD
Collect ACMG/AMP evidence and write candidate variant tables
Query tabix-indexed files by region, and read SAM/BAM/CRAM alignments and coverage
notes: pysam includes htslib, and pysam.samtools / pysam.bcftools wrap those tools as Python functions, but there are no samtools, bcftools or tabix commands.
Alignment, variant calling and VEP annotation (BWA-MEM2, GATK, VEP) are not installed; run them as AWS HealthOmics workflows.

environments.title: Single-cell analysis and trajectories
environments.description: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis and trajectories: Scanpy and AnnData (QC, normalization, PCA, neighbors, UMAP, Leiden clustering, marker genes), scVelo for RNA velocity, CellRank for cell fate and trajectory inference, and Squidpy for spatial transcriptomics.
use_for: Single-cell QC, normalization, highly variable genes, PCA, neighbors, UMAP and Leiden clustering with Scanpy
Marker genes and differential expression between clusters
RNA velocity from spliced and unspliced counts (loom or h5ad) with scVelo
Cell fate probabilities, terminal states and driver genes with CellRank
Spatial neighborhood enrichment, co-occurrence and spatial statistics with Squidpy
notes: The sandbox has no internet access, so the example datasets in scanpy.datasets, scvelo.datasets and squidpy.datasets cannot be downloaded. Write the user's data to the sandbox or simulate data.
